Citizen Registration
text:
Dress Code — Approved Citizen Aesthetic
Citizens are encouraged to dress as befits a Republic that abolished fast fashion. Earth tones. Natural fibres. Dystopian utility chic. Propaganda agency swagger.


🌿

Green Order


Olive, khaki, forest green. Military adjacency. The Covenant on your sleeve, literally or figuratively.



📋

Bureau Official


Grey suits, lanyards, clipboards. “I’m from the Ministry of Cultural Conformity and I need to see your permit.”



⛏

Rewilding Worker


Work boots, soil-stained canvas, high-vis with the Republic seal. Your three months are showing.



📡

GreenCast Correspondent


Microphone (prop), green lanyard, the specific expression of someone who has pre-cleared their questions.



🕯

Resistance (Undercover)


You look like a citizen. You have a pre-Republic road atlas hidden somewhere. You trust no one. Especially not that Sector Warden.



⚖

Tribunal Official


Dark robes, a gavel (prop), an expression of sincere ecological concern and zero flexibility.




Synthetic fabrics are theatrically prohibited. The Republic does not actually have jurisdiction over your wardrobe. Wear what you want. The propaganda is more fun if you play along.

title: Citizen Registration
text:
Ration Token Economy
The bar operates on ration tokens in true Republic style. Tokens are available at the Citizen Processing desk. One token = one drink. Additional tokens may be obtained by:

Successfully completing a Tribunal Re-enactment
Identifying contraband in the Black Market Corner
Denouncing a fellow citizen to a Bureau Official (theatrical only — no actual consequences unless they’re your mate and the bit goes on too long)
Correctly reciting a Covenant clause from memory
Providing an explanation for your pre-Republic carbon crimes that satisfies the Confession Booth operative

title: Citizen Registration
text:
The Tribunal — Participation Guide
The Extinction Tribunal will convene at intervals throughout the evening. Citizens may be called as defendant or prosecutor. The charges are fictional. The dramatic stakes are real.
Sample Charges: - “The defendant owned a Land Rover and used it for the school run” - “The defendant flew to Ibiza four times in a single year and called it ‘necessary’” - “The defendant lobbied against cycle lane expansion in their local council” - “The defendant kept using plastic bags even after they cost five pence”
Defence options: - Ignorance (weak, but traditional) - Necessary economic activity (the Republic has heard this one) - Personal carbon offsets (the Tribunal will laugh) - Throwing a co-conspirator under the rewilding tractor

title: Citizen Registration
text:
The Carbon Confession Booth
Unburden yourself. Tell the Booth Operative your greatest pre-Republic ecological sin. They will assess your carbon guilt on a scale of 1 (left the tap running) to 10 (owned an SUV with a personalised plate).
High scores receive a symbolic sentence — typically some form of theatrical penance performed in front of whoever is nearby.
All confessions are treated with the full gravity they deserve.

title: Citizen Registration
text:
Getting There — Citizens Are Reminded
The Emerald Republic has abolished private vehicles. We note that it has not actually done this, as the Republic is fictional. Nevertheless, the organisers prefer you:

Walk / cycle / take the train / share a vehicle
Not show up in a diesel SUV and expect ideological immunity because you’re wearing the right costume

This is partly carbon guilt and partly just parking.


Tonight is satire. Tonight is a party. Tonight we play at the world that almost was — or might yet be — and we laugh at it and we dance in it and we go home at the end.
The point of dystopian fiction is to look at where the logic leads. The eco-fascism thesis starts with “what if they were actually right about the emergency?” and then asks “and what if that made them stop caring about how they fixed it?” That’s the bit. That’s the horror. Not that they were wrong about the planet. That they might have been right, and done this anyway.
Think about it. Or don’t. There’s a Confession Booth and a Dance Floor and it’s Year II and the earth is, somehow, still here.
THE EARTH ENDURES. THE REPUBLIC ENDURES. YOU ARE PERMITTED TO ENJOY THIS.

title: The Chronicle of Necessary Events
section: Part I — The Age of Burning (Before Year Zero)
text:
Part I — The Age of Burning (Before Year Zero)
The world the old generation built was a furnace with a loyalty programme.
They knew. The reports came in for sixty years — meticulous, damning, increasingly desperate. Each report was filed. Each committee discussed it. Each summit produced a communiqué. The communiqués were filed next to the reports. The burning continued.
By the mid-2020s, the language of climate discourse had fractured into two dialects: the performative (“we are deeply committed to net zero”) and the operational (drilling permits, new airports, fossil fuel subsidies). The gap between them was measured in parts per million.
And then the activists came out of the tunnels.



2024 — 2026


The Movement Expands. What began as spray paint and road blockades becomes a distributed network of cells operating across 34 countries. Membership swells after the Marseille Heat Event kills 6,000 in a fortnight. The public mood shifts. The spray paint stays on the buildings longer before anyone bothers to remove it.




2027 — The Great Burning


Southern European wildfires combine with record Saharan heat to produce a climate refugee crisis involving 4 million people in eight weeks. The Italian government collapses. Spain declares emergency rule. The Iberian network — the largest coordinated cell of eco-activists on the continent — begins operating openly, no longer bothering to wear masks. Nobody arrests them. The police have been reassigned to manage the refugee flows.




2028 — The London Protocols


A hung Parliament, a constitutional crisis, and three successive Prime Ministers in four months create the conditions. The movement’s legal arm — by now staffed with barristers, economists, and one former cabinet minister who’d had enough — drafts the London Protocols: emergency climate governance legislation, radical in scope, technically legal. It passes on a vote of 221 to 218. The margin is three MPs who believe it will fail quickly and position them well for the resulting election. It does not fail.




2029 — The Emergence of The Verdant


No one knows the original name. That’s the point. A figure appears simultaneously across the movement’s distributed cells — same manifesto, same cadence, same willingness to say the unsayable. “We have been asking. We have been asking for fifty years. The asking is over.” Whether The Verdant is one person, a committee, or an AI trained on climate grief and revolutionary tracts remains classified under the Green Covenant’s Article 12 (State Security Through Productive Ambiguity).




2029 — The Green Unification


The cells coalesce into the Green Order over a single extraordinary fortnight. Broadcasting House is occupied — not stormed, occupied, with the building’s own security standing aside after a three-hour conversation about their children’s future. Parliament follows. The elected members are invited to continue meeting, under supervision, as an advisory body. Most do. The ones who don’t are not harmed. They are simply ignored, which feels worse.




Year Zero — The Declaration


The Emerald Republic is declared from the steps of what was once the Palace of Westminster. The Carbon Constitution is ratified within six weeks. It is 14 pages long — shorter than most terms-and-conditions agreements — and contains within it the legal architecture for everything that follows. Legal scholars will later note that it was, in its way, an elegant document. Several of those scholars are currently on sabbatical.




Year I — The Necessary Unpleasantness


The Republic implements. Carbon rationing. Travel permits. The Extinction Tribunals — at first presented as truth commissions, evolving, as these things do, into something with rather more teeth. The private vehicle ban. The Great Rewilding Labour Conscription (three months mandatory service per adult citizen, per year). GreenCast replaces the BBC. The old internet is throttled to 2010 speeds to reduce data-centre power consumption; the dark web thrives. Nostalgia for the old world becomes a Category C offence.




Year II — Now


The Republic endures. The Earth, one must admit, does appear to be breathing slightly better. At what cost is a question you may ask quietly, in private, among trusted friends. At a party, say. A themed party. Where everything is fictional. Yes.

title: The Chronicle of Necessary Events
section: Part II — The Verdant: A Portrait
text:
Part II — The Verdant: A Portrait

“I am not important. The carbon budget is important. I am merely the person who finally stopped being polite about it.” — The Verdant, First Address, Year Zero

What is known:

Appeared first as a pseudonymous author of the Extinction Manifesto (2026), which circulated on encrypted networks before being printed and left on the seats of trains across three continents
Voice: precise, unhurried, with the particular calm of someone who has already made peace with being called a monster
Never photographed without the Green Order’s sigil obscuring their face
Reportedly has strong opinions about compost
Two biographies have been attempted. One author is rewilding in Northumberland. The other recanted.

The cult of personality that has formed around The Verdant is, officially, discouraged. Unofficially, the murals are very good.

title: The Chronicle of Necessary Events
text:
Part IV — Rumours (Unverified, Officially Denied)

That The Verdant wept at the Declaration and had to be steadied by two Green Order lieutenants before finishing the speech
That the Carbon Constitution’s final clause — “And if this is not enough, we will do more” — was added at 3am and nobody has been sure what it means since
That somewhere, a resistance exists; that somewhere, people print forbidden maps of the old motorways and pass them hand to hand; that somewhere, someone has a car in a barn
That the Earth, recovering, is beautiful in ways it hasn’t been in living memory, and that this fact makes everything more complicated, not less

title: THE EMERALD REPUBLIC
text:
SUMMONS TO CITIZEN CELEBRATION
By order of the Cultural Conformity Bureau, the residents of Sector Warren are summoned to mark the Second Year of the Green Covenant with an evening of state-approved entertainment, communal reflection, and celebratory ration supplementation.
The Republic has endured. The Earth breathes. You are invited to dance on the grave of the old world.

“Two years ago, the skies over Parliament still burned with the fires of the old order. Two years ago, they said we were extremists. Tonight we are the government. Tonight we are the law. Tonight — we celebrate.”
— The Verdant, Second Year Address to the Green Assembly

title: THE EMERALD REPUBLIC
text:
WHAT TO EXPECT
The evening will proceed as all things proceed in the Emerald Republic: with purpose, with discipline, and with a great deal of fermented apple product from the approved collective orchards.
You will encounter:

The Museum of Necessary Unpleasantness — an exhibition of What Had To Be Done
The Tribunal Re-enactment Stage — citizen volunteers play both sides
The Carbon Confession Booth — unburden yourself of your pre-Republic sins
Approved Music — frequency-certified by the Ministry of Acoustic Standards
The Black Market Corner — contraband (props only, probably)
Sector Warden Impersonators — spot the real one, win a ration token


Citizens are reminded that this is a satirical fiction event. The Emerald Republic is not real. The Just Stop Oil people have not, to our knowledge, seized Parliament. Yet. Costume props representing state authority are props. No actual compliance is required. The Verdant is a fictional character. Carbon guilt is real and yours to manage independently.

title: THE EMERALD REPUBLIC
text:
THE WORLD YOU ARE ENTERING
When you step through the door, you step into Year II of the Emerald Republic.
The old world ended not with a bang but with a spreadsheet — a carbon audit so damning that three governments fell in a week. Into the vacuum stepped the movement everyone had dismissed as irritating roadblockers. They had a plan. They had cells in every city. They had The Verdant.
What followed was swift, ideologically coherent, and deeply unsettling to anyone who valued nuance.
The Republic asks only one thing of its citizens: compliance in the name of survival. How much compliance is never quite specified. That’s rather the point.

title: The Green Covenant
text:
Preamble
We, the survivors of the Age of Burning, who bore witness to the consequences of infinite appetite meeting a finite world, who watched the seas rise and the forests fall and the governments file the reports and schedule the follow-up meetings —
We, who were called extremists for insisting that arithmetic applies to the atmosphere —
We, who asked and asked and asked until the asking became insufficient —
Do hereby establish the Emerald Republic, and bind ourselves and all who dwell upon this recovered earth to the following Covenant. Not as ideology. Not as opinion. As physics.

title: The Green Covenant
text:
The Twenty Clauses


The Earth Is Not A Resource. The Earth is the condition of existence. It is not owned. It is not managed. It is inhabited, by permission, by those who demonstrate sufficient care. The Emerald Republic exists to enforce this permission structure.


Carbon Is The Currency Of Survival. Every human action has a carbon cost. Every carbon cost has a planetary consequence. The Republic shall maintain a Carbon Budget in perpetuity, and no law, no emergency, no convenience shall authorise its exceedance.


The Right To Consumption Is Conditional. Citizens retain the right to consume in proportion to the planetary budget divided by the population. No citizen may exceed their allocation. No citizen may transfer their allocation to any entity that will exceed it on their behalf.


Private Combustion Is Abolished. The private internal combustion vehicle, the private jet, the private gas boiler, the private anything that burns: abolished. Collectively-owned transport exists. It runs on time. It is sufficient.


The Great Rewilding Is Mandatory. Forty percent of the Republic’s land area shall be returned to ecological function by Year Ten. Citizens shall contribute no fewer than ninety days of rewilding labour per year. This is not punishment. This is participation. The distinction is important and will be explained to you again if necessary.


Accountability Is Retroactive. Those who knowingly perpetuated carbon criminality — executives, politicians, lobbyists, the architects of delay — shall answer to the Extinction Tribunals. That this is uncomfortable is acknowledged. That it is necessary is not subject to debate.


Information Shall Serve Survival. Media which obscures ecological truth, which manufactures doubt, which frames the survival of the biosphere as a matter of political opinion, is not journalism. It is sabotage. It will be treated accordingly. GreenCast provides all necessary information.


The Past Shall Not Be Mourned Publicly. Nostalgia for the Age of Burning — for its conveniences, its freedoms, its extraordinary waste — constitutes a form of ideological pollution. Citizens may feel what they feel. They may not perform regret for what we escaped.


Children Belong To The Future. All children in the Republic shall be educated in ecological citizenship from birth. The curriculum is the biosphere. The classroom is the rewilded field. The examination is whether the forest is still standing.


Efficiency Is The Highest Aesthetic. Beauty is what survives. Architecture, clothing, food, culture — all shall be evaluated first for ecological footprint, then for other qualities. Art that celebrates waste is not art. It is a confession.


The Collective Supersedes The Individual. The individual’s right to choose ends where the planet’s right to continue begins. This boundary shall be determined by the Green Assembly, annually, based on the latest atmospheric data. Citizens may petition. Citizens may not override.


Borders Shall Be Ecological, Not Political. The Republic recognises no nation-state boundary that contradicts ecological reality. Watersheds are jurisdictions. Forests are territories. The atmosphere is commons. Political borders that damage ecological ones shall yield.


Technology Must Justify Itself. No technology shall be deployed whose net carbon cost exceeds its carbon saving over a ten-year horizon. Data centres, cryptocurrency, fast fashion supply chains, most of what was called the attention economy: reviewed, reduced, in some cases eliminated. The servers that remain run cold.


Silence Is Participation. The citizen who says nothing when a neighbour burns, wastes, or consumes in excess is complicit in the burning, waste, and excess. The Republic does not require informers. It requires citizens who understand that the atmosphere cannot distinguish between the emissions of the guilty and the emissions of the merely convenient.


The Republic Does Not Apologise For What Was Necessary. History will judge. History always does. The Republic is not governed by the judgment of the future — it is governed by the physics of the present. If what was done was wrong, let the archive show it, and let the forest judge whether it was worth it.


Emergency Powers Are Not Temporary. The emergency is the condition of the age. The powers appropriate to the emergency are appropriate to the age. A sunset clause on survival is not a political document — it is a suicide note. The emergency powers are permanent until the emergency is resolved. The Republic shall determine when that is.


Dissent Shall Be Ecological. Citizens may disagree with any policy of the Republic. They may propose alternatives. They may organise. Their proposed alternatives must, however, achieve equivalent or superior ecological outcomes. Dissent that does not pass this test is not political speech. It is sabotage dressed as opinion.


The Verdant Speaks For The Earth. Pending the establishment of a permanent Green Assembly with confirmed electoral processes (see Appendix C for timeline, noting that Appendix C is a living document and the timeline is reviewed annually), executive authority resides with the office of The Verdant. This is a transitional arrangement. The transition is proceeding thoughtfully.


Joy Is Permitted. The Republic is not a punishment. The Republic is a correction. Citizens are encouraged to experience pleasure, connection, beauty, and festivity within the approved carbon budget. The forest is beautiful. The clean river is beautiful. The sky, recovering, is beautiful. Dance in it.


And If This Is Not Enough, We Will Do More. The Covenant is not the ceiling. It is the floor. Should the atmospheric data require it, the Republic shall act further. No act necessary for survival is outside the scope of this document. This clause was added at 3am on the final night of ratification. Everyone knew what it meant. Everyone signed anyway.




The Covenant above is a piece of satirical speculative fiction exploring what happens when legitimate ecological urgency becomes detached from democratic accountability. It is not an endorsement of authoritarianism, forced labour, show trials, or the suppression of dissent — all of which are bad, including when performed in the name of good causes.
The terrifying thing about well-written authoritarian documents is how internally consistent they are. This one is. That’s the bit to sit with.



“We did not want power. We wanted a liveable planet. The two turned out to be related. We are still deciding how we feel about that.”
— The Verdant, private correspondence, leaked Year I, authenticity disputed by the Ministry of Information (which is suspicious in itself)
